status: Viewed 11 Nov 2026: images 545, 549 and 609 at 1500 px, and every second image of 341-613 on contact sheets. Galt's cipher is a sign alphabet with a few numbers; on nearly every letter of 1622-25 the chancery wrote the plaintext in the margin beside the cipher passage (image 545 is one of these). On images 549 (postscript), 587 (slip) and 609 (points 6-11) no plaintext stands beside or over the cipher. No vetting block: the despatches are printed (Peder Galts depescher 1622-1624, ed. Nils Ahnlund, Historiska handlingar 26, Stockholm 1920; Libris 383507) and the edition could not be opened online, so whether it prints these passages in clear is not known. With the glossed leaves in the same unit the passages should read by key lookup in any case.
why: Reports of the first resident Danish envoy at Gustav II Adolf's court, in the years of the 1624 Danish-Swedish crisis.

title: Peder Juel (Danish resident in Stockholm): register of his outgoing letters with the secret passages entered in number cipher, no decipherment
correspondents: Peder Juel → chancellor Christen Thomesen Sehested, statholder Hannibal Sehested, Peder Vibe and others
shelfmark: Rigsarkivet (Copenhagen), Tyske Kancelli, Udenrigske Afdeling (TKUA), Speciel del, Sverige: Resident Peder Juels og Mogens Høegs gesandtskabsarkiver, Ekstraktprotokol over relationer, indlæg og andre udgående skrivelser 1647-49 (film label C.195)

Cipher seen on image 5 (book pp. 4-5: about 4 lines on p. 4 and 15 lines on p. 5), image 6 (p. 6: 4 lines), image 7 and image 61 (p. 115: 10 lines). status: Viewed 11 Nov 2026. A bound register ('Extract offver alle afgangne Missiver Breffve de anno 1647') in which the resident's secretary summarised each outgoing letter in Danish. Where the letter had a secret passage the register gives it in cipher, in dotted runs of numbers with nothing written over or beside them. Three number sets occur: to the chancellor, 20 Nov 1647, numbers 8-64 with 123, 124, 129, 158 and a few signs (p. 5); to Hannibal Sehested, 20 Nov 1647, numbers 3-32 with 86, 208 (p. 6); to Peder Vibe, 2 Sep 1648, numbers 1-32 with 212, 277, 339, 351, 401, 412, 426, 442, 446 (p. 115). Juel's original letters to the chancellor of 1648-49 in the same 8-64 cipher are deciphered between the lines (TKUA Sverige, Relationer 1645-60, unit 261575, images 115-135; image 117, 4 March 1648, seen), so that set should read by key lookup; no deciphered sibling was seen for the other two sets. Fryxell (1836) printed a Swedish abstract of this register from a copy in the Royal Library and says the letters themselves could not be found; he gives nothing for the cipher passages.
why: The resident's secret remarks on Queen Christina's court and the Swedish council in 1647-48, for letters whose originals are in part lost.

seen.cipher: Black-and-white microfilm of a narrow bound register. Danish summaries in a secretary hand; inside them dotted runs of one- and two-digit numbers with occasional three-digit numbers and a few signs. Nothing is written over the numbers and the wide outer column is empty beside them.

prior_art.edition: Fryxell, Handlingar rörande Sverges historia 1 (1836; archive.org handlingarrrand01fryxgoog, full text opened): pp. 86 ff. print a Swedish abstract of 'Extract offver alle afgangne Missiver Breffve de anno 1647' from the Rostgaard copy in the Royal Library (entries Nov 1647 to 1649) and of the letter register 1649-54; a note says the full letters could not be found. The entries for November 1647 give only the clear summary; no cipher passage is resolved or mentioned there.
prior_art.literature: Web searches (queries below) found only Fryxell's abstracts and general accounts of Christina's reign; no edition of Juel's despatches and nothing in Becker's Samlinger on archive.org (title search returned no item).

vetting.key_check: No key sheet is held here. A deciphered sibling exists for one of the three number sets: Juel's original letters to the chancellor of 1648-49 (TKUA Sverige, unit 261575, images 115-135) carry the plaintext between the lines in the same 8-64 cipher; image 117 (4 March 1648) was compared by eye, the table was not built and no passage of the register was read. The 3-32 and 1-32 sets have no sibling seen.
vetting.key_held: Deciphered sibling letters for the 8-64 set in TKUA Sverige unit 261575, images 115-135 (interlinear plaintext); no key table.
